shortcodes.note: Usage is counted from content, not from the registry, because $shortcode_tags only holds what this request registered. Tags flagged registered_here = false are either front-end only, or left behind by a plugin that is gone. Both matter for a migration. Credibility is separate and comes first: a tag is credible when it is registered, carries attributes, or has a matching closing tag. The rest are bracketed prose until a human says otherwise, so quote used_credible and read the unconfirmed list before repeating any of it.

blocks.note: Counted from block delimiters in content. Core blocks serialise without a namespace and port more or less mechanically; every namespaced name is a component someone has to rebuild. reusable_refs counts wp:block pointers, which must be resolved before an export, because the content lives in a separate wp_block post.

builders.note: by_content classifies each item from its own content, so one item can appear under two builders and "empty" means the content is not in post_content at all. Builders that store layout in meta only show up under by_meta_key, which is why both are reported.

field_model.note: field_paths is the number to estimate from. content_keys counts rows in the census, which double counts every ACF field (value plus an underscore-prefixed pointer with an identical item count, which is how acf_detected is established) and counts each repeater row as its own field. Collapsing row indices to _N_ undoes the second.

meta_keys.note: Key names and counts only, never values. The split is a convenience, not a filter: bookkeeping keys are listed too. in_rest means the key is registered with show_in_rest, which is what decides whether a REST export can see the field. Estimate from field_model.field_paths, not from the length of this list.

revisions.note: Revisions are excluded from every content count in this report, which is why they need their own: they are usually most of the database and almost never migrate. Check them against db_bytes before anyone concludes the site is large.

comments.note: State and type counts only. No author names, emails, IP addresses or comment bodies are read. Porting, dropping or moving these to a hosted service is a decision someone has to make.

authors.note: Counted from the post_author column. wp_users and wp_usermeta are never queried, so no names, logins or email addresses are read.

hierarchy.note: Depth 0 is a root. An orphan is a child whose parent is not in the migratable set, which means the parent is trashed or gone: the child still renders but its URL and its place in the tree are already broken.

menus.note: Menu names and item counts. Navigation has to be rebuilt by hand in any new CMS, so its size is the estimate, and broken items are work that can be dropped instead of ported.

media.note: SVG, PDF and video each need a different answer in a headless setup, so the mix matters more than the total. Which files are unreferenced is not measured here.

redirects.note: Row counts from the redirect plugins we have met. A site can also keep rules in .htaccess, at the CDN or in a plugin not listed here, so zero means "none of these", not "none".

slugs.note: A slug that appears under two post types is unique in WordPress, which separates them by URL prefix, and not unique in a CMS that keeps one flat document set. Each collision is a decision before import, not after.
